findings.title: IntoIter::drop double-frees elements when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: IntoIter::drop -> drop_non_singleton moves the backing ThinVec out of the iterator into a local `vec` (`let mut vec = mem::replace(&mut this.vec, ThinVec::new());`, line 2546) and then runs `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut vec[this.start..]);` (line 2547). The `len == 0` repair (`vec.set_len_non_singleton(0)`, line 2548) only happens after drop_in_place returns. If any element's Drop::drop panics, unwinding drops the local `vec`, whose ThinVec::drop runs `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut this[..])` over the full original length (line 1917) and deallocates. This re-drops every element that was already destroyed (and every element previously moved out by next(), which ptr::read at line 2513 already consumed), producing a double-drop/double-free of attacker-influenced element state. Reachable entirely in safe code: e.g. define `struct E; impl Drop for E { fn drop(&mut self) { panic!() } }`, then `let it = thin_vec![E, E].into_iter(); drop(it);` (or iterate partially first), and catch the panic; the allocator/memory of the elements is freed twice. Fixed upstream in 0.2.16 by a DropGuard that sets the length to 0 before drop_in_place can unwind.

findings.title: ThinVec::clear double-frees elements when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: `ThinVec::clear` runs `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut self[..]);` (line 1084) and only afterwards `self.set_len(0)` (line 1085). The length is therefore not repaired if an element's Drop panics mid-drop. When the panic unwinds, the ThinVec still reports its old length and still owns the already-dropped elements; its ThinVec::drop then executes `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut this[..])` over the full length again (line 1917) and deallocates, double-dropping the elements. Reachable in safe code: `let mut v = thin_vec![BadElem(1), BadElem(0xbadbeef)]; v.clear();` with a Drop impl that panics on one element; the surviving vector is destructed again during unwinding (or after catch_unwind), freeing the elements twice. Fixed upstream in 0.2.16 with a DropGuard that zeroes the length even on panic.
